title: Monetary Policy and Economic Developments
summary: This Federal Reserve annual report excerpt reviews U.S. monetary policy and economic developments from 2018, documenting two rate hikes in H2 2018 that brought the federal funds target range to 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent, followed by a shift to a patient stance at the January 2019 FOMC meeting in response to softer global growth and muted inflation. The labor market strengthened with unemployment near 4 percent and payrolls averaging 224,000 per month, while PCE inflation fell to 1.7 percent and GDP growth reached approximately 3 percent for the year. key_points: FOMC raised the federal funds target range twice in H2 2018, bringing it to 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent following the December meeting
FOMC signaled patience at January 2019 meeting given softer global conditions and muted inflation pressures
Unemployment rate averaged just under 4 percent; payroll employment grew at 224,000 per month since June 2018
PCE inflation declined to 1.7 percent in December 2018 from slightly above the 2 percent target earlier in the year
Real GDP growth reached just under 3 percent for 2018, a pickup from recent years

Financial stability: U.S. financial system remains substantially more resilient than pre-crisis; asset valuations eased, capital ratios at historical highs, but business debt elevated and credit standards deteriorated in some segments
